title: Apple PCC startup archive processing lacked path confinement

cwe_mappings.note: Researcher explicitly identifies the path-traversal weakness class.

summary: Sentry documents a USD 150,000 award to Drinor Selmanaj for CVE-2026-20685.
root_cause: Privileged startup archive handling did not adequately confine output paths; mutable configuration could undermine runtime integrity assumptions.
impact: Researcher demonstrated configuration changes and telemetry disclosure in Apple’s virtual environment. Apple confirms potential sensitive-information leakage from a privileged network position.
defensive_takeaways: Confine archive output and authenticate provisioning inputs.
Include security-relevant mutable configuration in integrity review.
Use the fixed PCC release and preserve the vendor’s impact prerequisites.

reward.evidence_location: Article opening; researcher-hosted award-offer image provides corroboration
reward.notes: Individual CVE award attributed to Selmanaj. Researcher-hosted Apple offer is not vendor-hosted payment confirmation. USD follows official program context; cash settlement and award date are unverified.

published.note: Sentry’s own article listing supplies the date.

public_disclosure.note: CVE publication timestamp; detailed researcher article appeared later.

fixed.note: Apple identifies PCC Release 5E290.3 as fixed; exact release/deployment date was not established.

sources.title: Beyond Prompt Injection: Hacking Apple's Private Cloud Compute
sources.author: Drinor Selmanaj / Sentry

sources.title: Apple CNA record for CVE-2026-20685
sources.author: Apple CNA, distributed through the CVE Program

sources.title: Apple Security Bounty US-dollar program context
sources.author: Apple Newsroom

verification.method: Read the researcher article, publication index, full Apple-authored CNA record and official currency context; reviewed the researcher-hosted offer graphic.
limitations: Research was demonstrated in Apple’s virtual environment; production was not tested by the researcher.
No confirmed production prompt-content leakage is claimed here.
Award attribution is researcher-hosted; vendor CNA evidence corroborates the vulnerability and fixed version, not payout.
No exact report, award, fix deployment or payment date was established.
